findings.title: User authorization does not bind fee_recipient or fee_amount

failing_checks.title: Recipient binding
failing_checks.reason: The signed args omit fee_recipient. The recipient is caller-chosen and is not checked against any allowlist, so a relayer can redirect the fee up to max_fee_amount.

failing_checks.title: Soroban contract checks
failing_checks.reason: The user's auth covers only fee_token, max_fee_amount, expiration_ledger and the target call. It does not cover fee_recipient or fee_amount. failing_checks.title: Verification of incoming authentication
failing_checks.reason: The user's signed auth payload covers fee_token, max_fee_amount, expiration, target and args. It leaves out fee_recipient. A relayer can therefore pick any recipient, up to max_fee_amount, and the signature still verifies.

failing_checks.title: Stated purpose versus behaviour
failing_checks.reason: The README says the user signs the authorization and that the relayer verifies the fee recipient. The authorized args cover fee_token, max_fee_amount, expiration and the target call, but not fee_recipient. The signed payload also does not bind fee_amount, though the cap does bound it.
